label: D1 after unrewarded S2 visit, largest after a1->S2 rare-unrewarded; scaled by a1 lean
terms: (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S2 u") ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a2 S2 u") ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a2 S2 u") * choice ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == -1) * (in_rew == 0) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == -1) * (in_rew == 0) * choice
explanation: Active only at D1. Magnitude is set by the previous trial: large (~+4.8 above baseline) after a1 -> S2 (rare) unrewarded, moderate (~+1.6) after a2 -> S2 (common) unrewarded, and near zero after any rewarded trial or any S1 visit. So it signals unrewarded S2 visits, which a model-based agent reads as evidence for switching to a1. After a2 S2 u its size goes up with the models a1-leaning policy logit (choice) at D1. On the windows first trial (previous trial outside the window), no-reward input combined with the a1 lean stands in for this. Two last-trial indicators alone reach dev R^2 0.68; all five terms reach dev 0.84 beyond timing. The trial before, the hidden good state, time since reversal and value add little. No future variables used; choice is the models own current logit.

issues: The claim that the score is 'at the ceiling' is wrong. The original terms leave a systematic over-prediction of about -0.46 at D1 after every pattern other than S2-unrewarded (misses: D1 after a1 S2 r -0.464, a1 S1 u -0.464, a1 S1 r -0.463, a2 S1 u -0.462, ...). The timing baseline (~0.64 at D1) is a mean over all D1 steps, and no term removes it for the windows where the feature is actually ~0. Adding one offset term, (phase == D1) * (prev_state != -1), raises test R^2 beyond timing from 0.836 to 0.909, well above the additive 'all' ceiling of 0.83.

The worst remaining errors are on a window's first trial. The 'no-reward input x a1 lean' stand-in predicts ~3.9 where the actual value is 0 in several windows (the unseen previous trial was probably an S1 or common visit). Even after the fix, D1 after '?' is over-predicted by about -0.42. This is an inherent limit of the window data, not a mistake in the label.

The factual claims check out on test. The feature fires only at D1 (GO and D2 residuals are 0). It is large after a1 S2 u (weight +4.79, residual +4.61) and moderate after a2 S2 u (+1.6, residual +1.19). It is near zero after rewarded trials and S1 visits (residual about -0.64, which is minus the baseline). The two last-trial indicators reach test 0.677. The a2 S2 u x choice term is real: dropping it from the improved set lowers test R^2 from 0.915 to 0.871. An a1 S2 u x choice term adds a little (0.836 -> 0.845). The explanation uses no future variables.
